# Flags

**Generated by `pnpm flags:docs`. Do not edit by hand.**

Source: `packages/shared/src/flags.ts` and `packages/shared/src/status.ts`.

There are exactly two kinds of flag (§5.1). Nothing outside the registry may build
one from a string literal.

## Statuses

Every one of these means something different. Collapsing any of them into
`no_result` turns "we could not look" into "there is nothing there".

| status           | meaning                                                        |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `has_result`     | The source ran and found something.                            |
| `no_result`      | The source ran and found nothing. It looked.                   |
| `low_confidence` | The source found something it does not trust enough to assert. |
| `error`          | The source failed. It did NOT look.                            |
| `timeout`        | The source ran out of time. It did NOT finish looking.         |
| `unavailable`    | The source is not configured or is down. It did NOT look.      |
| `skipped`        | The source was deliberately not run. It did NOT look.          |
| `not_executed`   | The run never reached this source at all.                      |

## Derived flags

Mechanically `${source}_${status}`, one row per source, one column per status.
All of them are legal; which ones a given source can actually emit depends on what
that source does.

## Aggregate flags

Conclusions drawn ACROSS sources — a judgement, not a status, which is why no
source/status pair produces them and why they are hand-registered.

| flag                     |
| ------------------------ |
| `local_result_found`     |
| `no_local_result`        |
| `local_low_confidence`   |
| `local_incomplete`       |
| `exact_full_match`       |
| `exact_partial_match`    |
| `exact_ambiguous`        |
| `variant_text_detected`  |
| `input_reordered`        |
| `agent_budget_exhausted` |
| `agent_model_failed`     |
| `final_answer_uncited`   |
| `llm_failover`           |
| `usage_unavailable`      |
| `model_has_result`       |
